subject: Edge-affinity override and regional failover playbook — action items for impacted customers
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge-affinity override and regional failover playbook — action items for impacted customers

Hi Samantha —

Quick note from the incidents desk: earlier this morning (09:02 UTC) we observed a sustained peering disruption affecting select EU and APAC cloud edges (notably eu-west-1 and apac-southeast-1) that resulted in elevated error rates and increased tail latency. The serving plane automatically initiated failover to our US edge pools for active requests where compatible model variants were available.

What we did (summary):
- Automatic routing fallback enabled at 09:05 UTC; traffic routed to nearest healthy US pools
- Short-lived connection resets were observed between 09:02–09:20 UTC; overall request success recovered to baseline by 09:25 UTC
- No scheduled config changes were made; this was a network/peering event at the cloud provider level

Immediate customer-facing guidance (please action):
1) If you're sensitive to region residency, flip the region-preference header to your preferred target (e.g., X-Redwood-Region: us) or call endpoints explicitly scoped to us (api.us.redwood.ai) — this forces deterministic affinity while we stabilize EU/APAC routing.
2) If you use short DNS TTLs to prefer edge affinity, consider increasing TTL to 60s for the next 48 hours during stabilization.
3) For HTTP clients: enable our region-fallback header handling (see attached "reroute-instructions.pdf") to let the SDK gracefully retry to the fallback pool without client-level timeout storms.
4) Optional: opt-in to our temporary SMART-BRIDGE routing policy if you want automatic traffic mirroring to a secondary region for verification (contact account team to enable).

Data residency note: we did not migrate persisted customer data; inference payloads were proxied through US edges while failover was active. For customers with strict egress/KMS constraints, we will provide audit logs and a scoped timeline — please let us know if you require an official attestation.

Attachments: reroute-instructions.pdf (quick config snippets, SDK examples)

If you'd like, Marissa and I can run a 30-minute war-room with your NetOps to walk through quick config changes and confirm your routing preferences.

Connor
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0192

Thanks Connor — really appreciate the rapid heads-up. Couple quick questions from our side: 

1) Do you have a short statement we can share with our compliance team on whether any PII or long-term storage was transferred between regions during the failover?
2) Our NetOps asks whether session affinities were preserved for existing conversations (we run multi-turn chat flows and don't want to lose context).
3) If we apply the region-preference header, will that create an availability hole for EU users while DNS and cloud edges stabilize?

We can take the 30-minute session — can you do 11:00 PDT today? NetOps has a maintenance window then and will be available.

-Sam
Director of Platform — Acme AI

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge-affinity override and regional failover playbook — action items for impacted customers

Hi Sam — thanks for the questions; I’ll answer each point and outline what we’ll provide after the call.

1) Data residency / PII: No customer-sourced persisted data was migrated between regions. During failover, inference payloads were routed through US edges but not persistently stored. For formal compliance evidence we will provide:
   - A signed incident attestation (scope: request proxying; no persistent storage changes)
   - Per-tenant request timeline logs for 2025-06-10 08:50–09:30 UTC (CSV extract attached: audit-request.csv)

2) Session affinity: active KV caches for multi-turn sessions were preserved where model variant compatibility existed; however, if your setup pinned specific region-only model weights, a small fraction of sessions required state rehydration from client side. We will provide a per-session flag in the CSV where rehydration occurred so you can correlate.

3) Region-preference header impact: forcing region preference to 'us' will direct new requests to US pools and could increase latency for EU users temporarily. If low latency for EU users is critical, we recommend a selective policy: set region-preference on server-side endpoints that serve internal back-office traffic while leaving end-user endpoints with normal affinity.

Action items I’m committing to before 16:00 PDT today: 
- Deliver signed incident attestation document (Olga)
- Produce per-tenant timeline CSV (attached: audit-request.csv)
- Join 11:00 PDT war-room (Connor + Marissa + Olga) and run through SDK toggles and region-preference examples

Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Postmortem actions and middle-of-week status for Acme follow-up

Team — quick postmortem update based on yesterday's war-room and artifacts we pushed to the Drive. Consolidated actions and ETA: 

1) Attestation & logs: Olga delivered the signed attestation and the CSV export; I uploaded both to the Drive folder and linked to INFRA-7421.
2) SDK snippets: Connor delivered a 1-page example (region header + retry best-practices). I reviewed and requested a small tweak for the Node example (PR #183). ETA for final snippet: 2025-06-12 10:00 PDT.
3) SMART-BRIDGE opt-in: Ben enabled opt-in for Acme at 12:30 PDT; we observed a small increase in cross-region probes for verification traffic but no errors. I left monitoring alarms in place (threshold: 2% error over 5m).
4) Compliance request: Acme asked for a formal post-incident Q&A; Olga to coordinate with Legal for the final wording.

Open items (owners):
- Legal attestation review (OLGA + Legal) — due 2025-06-13
- Node SDK example tweak (CONNOR) — PR #183 review and merge — due 2025-06-12 10:00 PDT
- Close INFRA-7421 after we attach final artifacts (BEN) — target close 2025-06-16

I also started a short root-cause thread with Network Eng (INFRA-7440) to capture why peering resets occurred; initial hypothesis: transient route flap during provider BGP maintenance window. Will share update when engineering confirms.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Engineering — Redwood Inference
